rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reading makes the Book the decree written for creation concerning felicity, wretchedness, lifespan, and provision; no one can alter it.
rows.anchor: قيل : ذلك الكتاب الذي كتبت على الخلق بالسعادة والشقاوة والأجل والرزق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading makes the Book God's love and knowledge inscribed in the hearts of His friends, with contentment toward the events of His decree.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ذلك الكتاب الذي كتبت في قلوب أوليائي من محبتي ومعرفتي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The Book is the covenant to the Beloved and place of the secret; the Prophet knows revelation's mysteries, and saints and truthful ones after him love its subtleties.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ذلك الكتاب الذي كتبت في قلوب أوليائي من محبتي ومعرفتي في الرضا بموارد قضائي ، والكتاب هو العهد إلى الحبيب وموضع السر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further reading is the pre-eternal divine pledge that God's mercy preceded His wrath.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ذلك الكتاب الذي كتبت على نفسي في الأزل ' إن رحمتي سبقت غضبي '

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: There is no doubt for the person whose secret God opens and whose heart He adorns with understanding from Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل لا ريب فيه : لا شك فيه لمن فتحت سره وزينت قلبه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: There is no doubt for the person whose secret is purified by the light of insight into the text's subtle meanings.
rows.anchor: وقيل لا ريب فيه : لمن طهرت سره بنور الاطلاع على لطائف معانيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the people of gnosis, the Book is true guidance and an added clarification.
rows.anchor: حقا لأهل المعرفة وزيادة بيان وهدى

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl calls it clarification for someone who magnifies his own affairs, power, and strength.
rows.anchor: وقال سهل : بيان لمن تكبر أمر حوله وقوته

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd reads the guidance as connection for those cut off from created entities.
rows.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله : هدى للمتقين ، وصلة للمنقطعين عن الأعيان

rows.speaker: أبو يزيد
rows.claim: Abu Yazid defines the God-fearing person as one who speaks and acts for God.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو يزيد رحمه الله : المتقي من إذا قال : قال لله

rows.speaker: الداراني
rows.claim: Al-Darani defines the God-fearing as those whose hearts have been stripped of love for desires.
rows.anchor: وقال الداراني : المتقون الذين نزع من قلوبهم حب الشهوات

none: A bare heading quoting the next verse, with no commentary.

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some gloss the command to worship your Lord as a command to affirm His oneness.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : وحدوا ربكم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others call for worship purified of partners, teaching that divine oneness and sincerity lead to God-consciousness.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : أخلصوا عبادة ربكم من غير اتخاذ الشريك فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse teaches the path of spiritual poverty: earth is a place to tread, sky a covering, water wholesome, and plants food; do not worship creatures for worldly needs, since God provides necessities without making you indebted to anyone.
rows.anchor: أعلمكم في هذه الآية سبيل الفقر بأن يجعل الأرض وطئا والسماء غطاء والماء طيبا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The reproach is read as demanding from people the realities of spiritual meanings while lacking their outward observance oneself.
rows.anchor: قيل فيه : أتطالبون الناس بحقائق المعاني وأنتم خالون من ظاهر رسومها

words: قَدْ نَرَىٰ تَقَلُّبَ وَجْهِكَ فِى ٱلسَّمَآءِ
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: God first taught the Prophet that he belonged to the Truth so he would observe its etiquette; his confident gaze toward heaven was answered in keeping with his wish.
rows.anchor: قيل فيه أعلمه أولا أنه من الحق ليكون متأدبا بآداب الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After granting the Prophet's wish, God teaches that His own will is to transfer him to the Kaaba and establish it as qibla for him and his community; the Prophet's pleasure never departs from God's pleasure.
rows.anchor: أخبره بعد أن أجابه إلى مراده

rows.speaker: بعض العراقيين
rows.claim: An Iraqi Sufi says the body should face the Kaaba outwardly while the heart remains turned toward witnessing God: the Kaaba is the body's qibla and God the heart's.
rows.anchor: قال بعض العراقيين : ترسم معهم برسم الظاهر في استقبال الكعبة ببدنك

rows.speaker: القاسم
rows.claim: Al-Qasim reads the declaration as calling the afflicted to accept God's allotment and patiently bear trial.
rows.anchor: قال القاسم : هذه إشارة تدعو إلى الرضا بالقسمة والصبر على المحنة

rows.speaker: القاسم
rows.claim: Al-Qasim says every ordeal conceals blessing and the lights of blessing conceal the fires of love; he praises acceptance of events that neither piety nor disobedience can reverse.
rows.anchor: قال القاسم : هذه إشارة تدعو إلى الرضا بالقسمة والصبر على المحنة . قال : تحت كل محنة نعمة وتحت كل أنوار النعمة نيران المحبة

words: وَإِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِى عَنِّى فَإِنِّى قَرِيبٌ
rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl calls modesty before God the lowest station of spiritual nearness.
rows.anchor: قال سهل : أدنى مقامات القرب الحياء من الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: النصرآباذي
rows.claim: Al-Nasrabadi says worship is assigned fixed times so servants can prepare with outward disciplines, while gnosis has no set time lest the heart cease its watchful witnessing.
rows.anchor: قال النصرآباذي : وقت الله عز وجل العبادات بأوقات ليتأهب العبد لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call means: turn toward God, people of sound understanding, and understand what He teaches.
rows.anchor: أقبلوا علي أصحاب الفهوم السليمة واعقلوا عني

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti identifies these people as an elite within the elect, inaccessible to the common people.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي : هم من الخصوص خصوص لم يجعل للعموم فيهم طريقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided them to remembrance and made them among its people, after they had been astray from remembering Him.
rows.anchor: إلى ذكره وجعلكم من أهله

rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: Ja'far glosses the vowed child as freed from the bondage of the world and its people.
rows.anchor: قال جعفر رحمه الله : عتيقا من رق الدنيا وأهلها

words: نَذَرْتُ لَكَ مَا فِى بَطْنِى مُحَرَّرًۭا
rows.speaker: محمد بن علي
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ali says the child is to be God's sincere servant; whoever is wholly God's is free from everything besides Him.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن علي رحمه الله في قوله تعالى : ﴿ نذرت لك ما في بطني محررا ﴾ أي : يكون لك عبدا مخلصا

rows.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Sahl defines the liberated person as one freed from personal aims and following caprice.
rows.anchor: سئل سهل بن عبد الله عن المحرر قال : هو المعتق من إرادات نفسه

words: نَذَرْتُ لَكَ مَا فِى بَطْنِى مُحَرَّرًۭا
rows.speaker: النوري
rows.claim: Al-Nuri reads the vow as freeing the mother from preoccupation with and management of the child, surrendering the child to God's wise direction.
rows.anchor: قال النوري - تغمده الله برحمته - في قوله تعالى :

rows.speaker: محمد بن الفضل
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl says the child is freed from being occupied with earning a livelihood.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن الفضل رحمه الله في قوله تعالى :

rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: Ja'far says God accepted Mary so greatly that even prophets of high rank would marvel at her standing; Zechariah's question and her reply point to the One who accepted her.
rows.anchor: قال جعفر : تقبلها حتى تعجب الأنبياء مع علو أقدارهم

words: فَتَقَبَّلَهَا رَبُّهَا بِقَبُولٍ حَسَنٍۢ وَأَنۢبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا حَسَنًۭا
rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti distinguishes outward and inward: in religious law God attributes goodness to Mary, while in reality He protects and nurtures her Himself.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمه الله : بقبول حسن : محفوظة

none: A bare heading quoting part of the verse, with no commentary.

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata says God grants a servant an elevated spiritual state only through obedience, sincere worship, and remaining in the prayer niche.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : ما فتح الله تعالى على عبد من عبيده حالة سنية إلا باتباع الأوامر

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti reads standing in the prayer niche as the heart's struggle against the lower self and its desires.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي : ﴿ وهو قائم يصلي ﴾ سره بمحاربه نفسه وهواه

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان
rows.claim: Abu Uthman calls the prayer niche a doorway to every good, a place where supplication is answered, and a path to intimacy; neglecting it closes the door.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : المحراب باب كل بر وموضع الإجابة

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says attachment to anything other than the One directly found is worship from the very source of reality.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي : من تمسك بغير الوجدانية بل بغير الواجد

words: وَلَهُۥٓ أَسْلَمَ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ طَوْعًۭا وَكَرْهًۭا
rows.speaker: الحسين
rows.claim: Al-Husayn says God draws creatures away from witnessing their own signs through special disclosure: beholding the Essence brings willing and unwilling submission, while beholding awe brings unwilling submission.
rows.anchor: قال الحسين : أخذهم عن شهود شواهدهم بخصائص الإطلاع عليهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One gloss says God prescribes servanthood with knowledge of people's weakness and ignorance.
rows.anchor: قيل : يعني يقال العبودية لعلمه بضعفكم وجهلكم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another says God intends to lighten the immense trust people burdened themselves with through ignorance.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يريد الله أن يخفف عنكم ما حملتموه بجهلكم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A person is weak in judgment and reason, except when God gives the light of certainty; strength comes through certainty, not from the self.
rows.anchor: قيل : ضعيف الرأي ضعيف العقل إلا من أمره الله بنور اليقين

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl says the judgment is by the wisdom God taught the Prophet in the Quran and religious law.
rows.anchor: قال سهل : بما علمك الله من الحكمة في القرآن والشريعة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reading says to judge by what God unveils directly, not merely by what people show outwardly, since the Prophet's vision is unveiling and direct witnessing.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لتحكم بين الناس بما أراك وأظهره لك

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata says the Prophet sees through God, speaks from God, and remains always within God's sight and hearing.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء في هذه الآية : بما أراك الله فإنك بنا ترى وعنا تنطق

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says direct encounter enabled the Prophet to bear the divine Essence after bearing the Attributes, whereas Moses bore the Attributes but not the Essence.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : إنما عظمت بالمباشرة فاحتمل الذات بعد ما احتمل الصفات

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Someone says the Prophet was favored pre-eternally yet may stumble in the witnessed moment; after reproach, as in 9:43, he returns to the favor decreed for him before time.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : فضلت في الأزل بالفضائل وقد تغتر في المشاهد العثرة

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd glosses the teaching as making the Prophet know his own worth.
rows.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه : عرفك قدر نفسك

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd divides knowledge into gnosis, expression, servanthood, and service, and says the Prophet received their greatest share.
rows.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه : عرفك قدر نفسك وقال أيضا : العلوم أربعة

rows.speaker: أبو يزيد
rows.claim: Abu Yazid divides knowledge into explanatory knowledge and knowledge of proof.
rows.anchor: قال أبو يزيد : العلم علمان : علم بيان وعلم برهان

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl distinguishes believers who know God but not His commands or days, scholars who know God and His commands but not His days, and prophets and truthful ones who know all three.
rows.anchor: قال سهل : العلماء ثلاثة : عالم بالله لا عالم بأمر الله ولا بأيام الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One gloss says God taught the Prophet hidden secrets known only through God Himself.
rows.anchor: وقيل : علمتك من مكنون أسراري ما لم تعلمه إلا بي

rows.speaker: أبو محمد الجريري
rows.claim: Abu Muhammad al-Jurayri says scholars see outward features and excellences, sages see inward features and defects, and spiritual elders see essences and realities.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو محمد الجريري : الأدلة ثلاثة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another classification names four scholars by their share: God Himself, knowledge and gnosis of God, the journey to the afterlife, or knowledge of that journey.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : العلماء أربعة : عالم حظه من الله الله

none: A bare heading quoting a neighboring verse, with no commentary.

rows.speaker: ممشاد الدينوري
rows.claim: Memshad al-Dinawari assigns Adam's sin to greed, Iblis's to pride, and Cain's to envy: greed deprives, pride humiliates, and envy abandons its victim.
rows.anchor: قال ممشاد الدينوري : كان معصية آدم من الحرص

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl says piety and sincerity are the heart's receptacles for the limbs' deeds.
rows.anchor: قال سهل : التقوى والإخلاص محلا القلوب لأعمال الجوارح

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata identifies the pious as those sincere to God in what they say and do.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : المخلصين له فيما يقولون ويعملون

rows.speaker: السلامي
rows.claim: Al-Sulami says offerings differ, but the nearest is the act God has promised to accept; that promise is truthful, and prostration is the place of nearness through remembrance.
rows.anchor: قال السلامي : القرابين مختلفة وأقرب القرابين ما وعد الله جل وعز بقبوله

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: On the neighboring warning not to grieve over those rushing into disbelief, al-Wasiti says God gives instruction upon instruction and denies them a share in the afterlife by employing them in their own ruin.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي : تعليما بعد تعليم

none: A bare heading quoting a neighboring verse, with no commentary.

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl says repentance has stations and states, and true repentance is the alliance with God and His Messenger described in this verse.
rows.anchor: قال سهل : التوبة لها مقامات وحالات

rows.speaker: القاسم
rows.claim: Al-Qasim says alliance with God proceeds through alliance with His Messenger, which proceeds through alliance with exemplary elders among God's servants; honoring them is required for progress in divine alliance.
rows.anchor: قال القاسم : موالاة الله مشتقة من موالاة رسوله وموالاة الرسول مشتقة من موالاة السادة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says that honoring an aged Muslim is part of honoring God's majesty.
rows.anchor: فإن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ' من تعظيم جلال الله إكرام ذي الشيبة المسلم ' ،

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says revering elders is part of reverence for God.
rows.anchor: وقال : صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' بجلوا المشايخ فإن تبجيل المشايخ من إجلال الله '

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl says God's party overcomes its own lower desires, wishes, and aims.
rows.anchor: وقال سهل في قوله : ﴿ فإن حزب الله هم الغالبون ﴾ قال : لأهوائهم وإراداتهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Others define God's party as His elect, steadfast with Him under the conditions of uprightness.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : حزب الله أهل خاصته والقائمون معه على شرائط الاستقامة

none: A bare heading quoting a neighboring verse, with no commentary.

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the servant's highest station is to acknowledge complete insolvency and return to God empty of all acts of obedience.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : أجل مقامات العبد إظهار إفلاسه والرجوع إليه خاليا من جميع طاعاته

rows.speaker: أبو حفص
rows.claim: Asked what he could bring before God, Abu Hafs answered that a poor person can offer only poverty to the Rich; he reads arriving alone as being empty of works, states, and devotions.
rows.anchor: قيل لأبي حفص : بماذا تقدم على الله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One Sufi reading assigns each created form a mode of life: hearts live by witnessing, selves by existence, servants by their worshipped Lord, the elect by sincerity, the afterlife by knowledge, and worldly life by ignorance, construction, and delusion.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : أبدع الله الهياكل وأظهرها على أخلاق شتى وصور مختلفة

rows.speaker: أبو حفص
rows.claim: Abu Hafs says God's command to prostrate before Adam showed that He needs no worship: creation's worship adds nothing to His kingdom, for He is mighty before creation, after its destruction, and at resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حفص : عرف الملائكة استغناءه عن عبادتهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One view distinguishes God's command to prostrate as an obligation from the command to leave as humiliation; the angels' prostration honored Adam and obeyed God.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : قوله لإبليس أمر تكليف وقوله

none: A bare heading quoting a neighboring verse, with no commentary.

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti warns that relying on ritual observances in both worlds makes ignorance a home, objection a trait, and distance from God its outcome; seeing worship as one's own act is dangerous self-regard.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : من استصحب كل نسك في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One explanation says Iblis saw his substance and worship and thought himself superior; self-regard in one's acts corrupts the soul.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : لما نظر إلى الجوهر والعبادة ظن أنه المسكين خير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another says Iblis's self-assertion alone brought the curse: nothing distanced him more than seeing himself.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لما قال إبليس : ' أنا ' قيل له : إن عليك اللعنة

words: أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِى مِن نَّارٍۢ وَخَلَقْتَهُۥ مِن طِينٍۢ
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further gloss says Iblis mistook created substance and origin for superiority, failing to recognize that merit comes from the Bestower rather than one's essence.
rows.anchor: وقيل في قوله ' أنا خير منه ' توهم أن الجوهر من الكون

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says wearing the garment of ritual practice makes the ego's claim of I arise; even without saying better, Iblis would have been ruined by asserting I in comparison.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : من لبس قميص النسك خاصره ' أنا '

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata says pride in himself veiled Iblis from revering God; when the Real dominates a heart, it leaves no room to exalt anyone else.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء في قوله : ' أنا خير منه ' : حجب إبليس برؤية الفخر بنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes God's curse from His curse: the possessive form denotes wrath continuously laid upon Iblis from eternity, while the definite form names what appeared then and increases until the respite ends.
rows.anchor: الفرق بينهما إذا قال : لعنتي أي سخطي الذي لم يزل مني جاريا عليك

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti warns that no one is safe from Iblis's fate: God met him with lights of protection while he was already under the reality of the curse, then suddenly disclosed what had been concealed.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : لا يأمنن أحد أن يفعل به كما فعل بإبليس

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One account lists five causes of Iblis's ruin: he did not admit or regret his sin, blame himself, regard repentance as required, or retain hope in mercy.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : لعن إبليس بخمسة أشياء شقي بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam was blessed with the opposite five traits: he admitted sin, regretted it, blamed himself, hurried to repent, and did not despair of God's mercy.
rows.anchor: وسعد آدم بخمسة أشياء : أقر على نفسه بالذنب ، وندم عليه ، ولام نفسه ، وأسرع في التوبة

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الداراني
rows.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Darani says Satan intended evil, yet his whisper became the cause of Adam's elevation; the lapse disciplined Adam and returned him to God's favor, as he confessed his wrong and sought God (7:23).
rows.anchor: قال أبو سليمان الداراني : وسوس لهما الشيطان لإرادة الشر بهما

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl describes whispering as a progression from natural disposition to the self, then thought and planning.
rows.anchor: قال سهل : الوسوسة ذكر الطبع ثم النفس ثم الهم والتدبير

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says Adam understood the prohibition to concern the particular tree indicated, while God intended its whole kind; he took another, and repented for failing to be cautious rather than for disobedience.
rows.anchor: قيل : أشار إلى جنس الشجرة

rows.speaker: الخراز
rows.claim: Al-Kharr az says the command and prohibition made Adam uneasy even in Paradise; God let the lapse occur so its lesson and proof would emerge, then expelled and reproached him, with 20:115 also cited.
rows.anchor: قال الخراز : والله ما هنىء آدم الجنة ولا سكناها

rows.speaker: الجنيد
rows.claim: Junayd reads the command as guarding the secret, raising one's aspiration, and being content with God in place of everything else.
rows.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمة الله عليه في هذه الآية : أمر بحفظ السر وعلو الهمة

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان
rows.claim: Abu Uthman defines qist as truthfulness.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : القسط الصدق

rows.speaker: رويم
rows.claim: Ruwaym says sincerity in supplication means ceasing to see one's own actions.
rows.anchor: قال رويم : إخلاص الدعاء أن ترفع رؤيتك عن أفعالك

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata defines sincere supplication as that which is free of afflictions and defects.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : إخلاص الدعاء ما خلص من الآفات

rows.speaker: حارث المحاسبي
rows.claim: Al-Harith al-Muhasibi says sincerity removes creatures from one's dealings with God.
rows.anchor: قال حارث المحاسبي : إخلاص الدعاء إخراج الخلق من معاملة الله

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان
rows.claim: Abu Uthman says sincerity is forgetting creatures while continually looking toward the Creator.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : الإخلاص نسيان رؤية الخلق لدوام النظر إلى الخالق

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another definition makes sincerity constant watchfulness and forgetting every self-serving interest.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : الإخلاص دوام المراقبة ونسيان الحظوظ كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation says Iblis began in disbelief but performed obedient acts before being returned to opposition, while the sorcerers began rightly, acted wrongly, and returned to their original state.
rows.anchor: أبدأ خلقة إبليس على الكفر والخلاف ثم استعمله بأعمال المطيعين

rows.speaker: الحسين
rows.claim: Al-Husayn says God's decree concerning deeds does not change, since actions may accord with or oppose a person's original nature.
rows.anchor: قال الحسين : في قوله : ﴿ كما بدأكم تعودون ﴾ لا تغيير لما أجرى عليه من الأعمال

none: A bare heading quoting a neighboring verse, with no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tests people with blessings to elicit gratitude and with trials to elicit patience; this group failed at both, showing neither gratitude in ease nor patience in hardship.
rows.anchor: قال : اختبرناهم بالنعم طلبا للشكر

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq contrasts hypocrites, who conceal one another's faults, with believers, who serve as mirrors through which one sees defects and receives correction aiding salvation.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق : المنافق ستر المنافق يستر عليه عوراته

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret the hypocrites' closed hands as withholding them from raising supplications and requests to their Patron; a report about the Prophet at the standing, with hand to chest like a beggar, and an accompanying poem illustrate the plea.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : يقبضون أيديهم عن رفعها إلى مولاها في الدعوات والحوائج

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes their closed hands as refusal to give charity.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يقبضون أيديهم عن الصدقة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further interpretation takes their closed hands as refusing to help Muslims.
rows.anchor: وقيل : يقبضون أيديهم عن معونة المسلمين

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl explains their forgetting God as forgetting His blessings, after which God makes them forget to give thanks for those blessings.
rows.anchor: قال سهل : نسوا نعم الله عندهم فأنساهم الله شكر النعم

none: A bare heading quoting the next verse, with no commentary.

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان
rows.claim: Abu Uthman says believers support one another in worship, spur one another to it, and strengthen one another on the path to salvation; he cites the Prophet's comparisons of believers to a building and to one body.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عثمان : المؤمنون أيضا يتعاونون على العبادة

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq says a believer naturally and instinctively befriends another believer.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق : المؤمن يوالي المؤمن طبعا وسجية

rows.speaker: أبو حفص
rows.claim: Abu Hafs defines stinginess as abandoning generosity when it is needed.
rows.anchor: سئل أبو حفص : ما البخل ؟

rows.speaker: حمدون القصار
rows.claim: Hamdun al-Qassar says whoever regards wealth as his own possession is miserly, since he keeps other people's hands away from it.
rows.anchor: قال حمدون القصار : من رأى لنفسه ملكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The secret is what only the Knower of secrets can see, while private conversation is what the recording angels can see.
rows.anchor: السر ما لا يطلع عليه إلا عالم الأسرار والنجوى ما يطلع عليه الحفظة

words: خُذْ مِنْ أَمْوَٰلِهِمْ صَدَقَةًۭ تُطَهِّرُهُمْ وَتُزَكِّيهِم بِهَا
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say taking their charity purifies them through zakat and from the stain of created things, while the Prophet's prayers settle them toward the afterlife and cut them off from worldly attachment.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : خذ منهم الصدقة فإن أخذك يطهرهم لإعطاء الزكاة

rows.speaker: رويم
rows.claim: Ruwaym reads purification and growth as cleansing their inner secrets and refining their souls.
rows.anchor: قال رويم : تطهر سرائرهم وتزكي نفوسهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One gloss takes the command to pray over them as a command to supplicate for them; the Prophet's prayer turns them toward the afterlife and away from the world.
rows.anchor: وقيل في قوله عز وجل : ﴿ وصل عليهم ﴾ : أي : ادع لهم

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says Hūd's state of connection and nearness made him fully present; his challenge to his opponents came from direct witnessing, seeing no one besides God.
rows.anchor: قال الواسطي : غلب على هود عليه السلام في ذلك الوقت الحال والوصلة والقربة

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says Lot's request for strength or refuge was ordinary human speech, expressing his awareness of his own state and preoccupation with his people.
rows.anchor: وقال في قصة لوط صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says Hūd spoke from direct witnessing, seeing no one besides God.
rows.anchor: وقال في هود : ﴿ فكيدوني جميعا ثم لا تنظرون ﴾ [ الآية : 55 ] . نطق عن مشاهدة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One gloss says Hūd challenges his opponents while held in God's grasp, might, and awe; plotting only reaches one captive to opposition.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : أي كيدوني بالحق من هو في قبضة الحق

words: مَّا مِن دَآبَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ ءَاخِذٌۢ بِنَاصِيَتِهَآ
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One reflection asks how anyone can claim independent standing when existence depends on another, and says that whoever says I contests God's grip.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : كيف يكون ذلك محل وأنت بغيرك قيامك

words: مَّا مِن دَآبَّةٍ إِلَّا هُوَ ءَاخِذٌۢ بِنَاصِيَتِهَآ
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another reflection says the verse invalidates self-claims: whoever asserts a claim wages war on divine power and contests God's grasp.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : فيه ذكر إبطال الدعاوى

none: A bare heading quoting a neighboring verse, with no commentary.
